meta.title: Social Media Image Sizes Reference Guide
meta.about_published_flag: published:false means the platform states no such size in any first-party documentation. The value is an observed convention that generally renders well, but it cannot be cited and may drift.

platforms.name: X (formerly Twitter)
platforms.note: X retired its Cards documentation when developer.x.com moved to docs.x.com — the old deep links now redirect to a generic overview and no replacement spec page exists. The card values below are the last officially published figures and can no longer be confirmed first-party.

also.label: display

also.label: display

assets.label: Cover Photo
assets.qualifier: 400 x 150 min; sRGB JPG under 100KB recommended
detail: Crops to 16:9 on desktop and 2.4:1 on mobile — keep key content centered

assets.label: Post Link Image (Open Graph)
assets.qualifier: 1.91:1; 600 x 315 min for the large render, 200 x 200 absolute min, 8MB max

also.label: minimum-for-feature

assets.label: App Icon
assets.qualifier: 512 x 512 to 1024 x 1024 accepted, under 5MB; JPEG / GIF / PNG
notes: 1024 x 1024 from the App Review submission guide ("Upload a 1024x1024 compliant app icon"). The 512-1024 range, 5MB cap and formats are stated in the Pages API create-an-app doc: https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/pages-api/create-an-app

assets.label: Feed Posts
assets.qualifier: Instagram keeps 320–1080 px wide as-is, downsizes anything larger
detail: Supported aspect range is 1.91:1 to 3:4 — i.e. 1080 x 566 (landscape) through 1080 x 1440 (max portrait)
1080 x 1350 (4:5) and 1080 x 1080 (1:1) are the common picks; anything outside the range gets cropped

assets.label: Stories & Reels
detail: Instagram accepts reels from 1.91:1 to 9:16; 9:16 fills the screen

platforms.name: Threads
platforms.note: The only first-party Threads media spec is the Threads API publishing doc: images 320 to 1440 px wide, up to 10:1, 8MB, JPEG/PNG; video max 1920 px wide, 9:16 recommended, 1GB, 5 minutes; carousels of 2 to 20 items. Pixel sizes below that the doc does not state are unpublished conventions.

assets.label: Post Image
detail: Threads API: 320 to 1440 px wide (scaled to fit), aspect up to 10:1, 8MB max, JPEG or PNG, converted to sRGB

assets.label: Carousel
assets.qualifier: images and videos can be mixed
notes: Was "up to 10 images, 1080 px wide each" (unpublished). The Threads API doc states carousels "must have at least 2 and no more than 20 total images, videos, or a mix of the two"; it gives no per-item size beyond the image and video specs.

assets.label: Video
detail: Threads API: 9:16 recommended, max 1920 px wide, 23 to 60 FPS, up to 5 minutes, 1GB max, MOV or MP4

sources.title: linkedin.com/help - photo won't upload to your profile (profile photo limits)

assets.label: Profile Photo
assets.qualifier: up to 7680 x 4320, 8MB max; PNG or JPG, no GIFs

assets.label: Link Preview (Open Graph og:image)
detail: Images less than 401 px wide display as a thumbnail
No file types are published for the sharing module

assets.label: Cover Image

notes: Was 4200 x 700 (verified 2026-07-24). As of 2026-11-02 answer a563309 lists "Page Cover image 1512 (w) x 256 (h) pixels" for both minimum and recommended.

assets.label: Company Post Images (with link)
detail: All page images: PNG or JPEG, 3MB max — LinkedIn recommends a high-res JPEG over PNG

assets.label: Profile Picture

also.label: alternate
also.description: practical upload size; YouTube states only the 98 x 98 render

assets.label: Channel Banner / Cover
assets.qualifier: 16:9 ratio; 2560 x 1440 recommended for TV; safe area 1235 x 338; 6MB max

also.label: safe-area
also.description: text and logos stay inside this on every device

assets.label: Video Thumbnail
assets.qualifier: 16:9, 640 px min width; 2MB max on mobile, 50MB on desktop

assets.label: YouTube Shorts Video
notes: YouTube documents Shorts as vertical with a maximum upload resolution of 1080p (answer 10059070) but publishes no pixel dimension.

platforms.name: Bluesky
platforms.note: Bluesky publishes no size doc, so the dimensions above are unpublished and derived from the app. The file limits are first-party: the AT Protocol lexicon caps post images at 2,000,000 bytes and the link-card thumbnail at 1,000,000 bytes, and accepts any image type for both. Profile avatar and banner are capped at 1,000,000 bytes, PNG or JPEG only.

sources.title: AT Protocol lexicon - app.bsky.actor.profile (avatar and banner)

assets.label: Profile Picture
notes: Dimensions are unpublished. max_bytes and formats come from app.bsky.actor.profile (accept image/png and image/jpeg, maxSize 1000000).

assets.label: Banner Image
notes: Dimensions are unpublished. max_bytes and formats come from app.bsky.actor.profile (accept image/png and image/jpeg, maxSize 1000000).

assets.label: Post Image
detail: Any image type, 2,000,000 bytes max (AT Protocol lexicon; formerly 1MB)
notes: Dimensions are unpublished. max_bytes and accepted types come from app.bsky.embed.images#image.image (accept image/*, maxSize 2000000), whose description says it was formerly limited to 1 MB.

assets.label: Landscape Link Preview
detail: Thumbnail: any image type, 1,000,000 bytes max (AT Protocol lexicon)
notes: Dimensions are unpublished. max_bytes and accepted types come from app.bsky.embed.external#external.thumb (accept image/*, maxSize 1000000).

assets.label: Portrait Link Preview
detail: Thumbnail: any image type, 1,000,000 bytes max (AT Protocol lexicon)
notes: Dimensions are unpublished. max_bytes and accepted types come from app.bsky.embed.external#external.thumb (accept image/*, maxSize 1000000).

assets.label: Standard Pin
assets.qualifier: 2:3 ratio; larger ratios get cut off in feed
detail: title: 100 char max - text box: 250 char max - description: up to 800 char
safe zones: 270 px top, 65 px left, 195 px right, 790 px bottom
file: BMP / JPEG / PNG / TIFF / WEBP, 20MB max on web

assets.label: Video Pin
assets.qualifier: 9:16 ratio; 4 seconds to 5 minutes, H.264 or H.265

assets.label: Avatar
assets.qualifier: max 10MB; JPEG / PNG / WEBP — GIFs go static

assets.label: Post Image
assets.qualifier: 2:3 dashboard view; displays up to 2048 x 3072 on click if no click-through link is set
detail: 20MB per image; 10 images per post in the apps, 30 on web

platforms.name: Medium
platforms.note: Medium has no published spec for profile or post-cover dimensions; the platform scales images to fit its display contexts.

assets.label: Post Image
assets.qualifier: below that, the full-width and outset placement options don't appear
detail: Max file size 25MB (.JPG, .JPEG, .GIF, .PNG)

assets.label: Profile Picture
assets.qualifier: under 1MB and smaller than 3000 x 3000; PNG / JPG / GIF
notes: Previously unpublished (500 x 500 was the identicon size). GitHub now states: "we recommend keeping the image at about 500 by 500 pixels."

platforms.name: Twitch
platforms.note: help.twitch.tv is a Salesforce app that frequently fails to render for automated checks; read it in a browser. Re-read in full 2026-08-03: the channel setup article now states dimensions only for the profile banner and info panels. The profile picture and video player banner sizes it used to carry are gone, so those are marked unpublished.

sources.title: emote formatting & instant emote upload requirements

assets.label: Profile Picture
notes: The channel setup article no longer states any profile picture dimensions. As of 2026-08-03 it says only: "Must be JPEG, PNG, or GIF and cannot exceed 10MB." The 800 x 800 upload and 256 x 256 display figures are long-standing convention that Twitch no longer documents.

assets.label: Profile Banner
assets.qualifier: scales to browser width; images are scaled to 480 high, so keep the artwork weighted left
notes: The 3MB cap previously recorded here is not stated in the article and was dropped 2026-08-03. The article gives the dimension only: "The recommended size for a profile banner is 1200x480px."

assets.label: Panel Images
assets.qualifier: under 2.9MB; larger images are resized to these maximums automatically

assets.label: Video Offline Banner
notes: Twitch documents no size for this. The channel setup article's "Upload a Video Player Banner" section gives steps only — and as of 2026-08-03 those steps are duplicated from the accent-colour section above it, so the article appears to have lost its banner instructions entirely. 1920 x 1080 remains the sensible upload size; it just cannot be cited.

assets.label: Subscriber Emoticons
assets.qualifier: PNG, under 100KB each in manual mode, or a single 112–4096 px square PNG under 1MB with auto-resize
detail: PNG format and the 112–4096 px auto-resize range come from the Emote Guidelines article; animated emotes are GIF, with a 512KB per-file cap in manual mode.
notes: Corrected 2026-08-03: this entry recorded a 512KB per-file cap, which is the animated-GIF figure. For standard emotes the guide states the three manual-mode files "must each be under 100KB".
